Rule R10: Never `BLOCK_ALL_CARDS`. unless at least two of the customer's cards show confirmed fraud or the customer's credentials are confirmed compromised.

Every one is a tiny authorisation, spread over days with no larger purchase after them, so they are not R5's sequence of three within an hour followed by a purchase.

20 other cards (20 other customers) newly show the same signature in the 30 days to the alert - 3+ online authorisations under $10, on a card that had not made such charges before - against 8 and 4 in the same window one and two months earlier: C05083-K1, C00348-K1, C09471-K2, C01326-K2, C03611-K2, C04105-K2, C04528-K1, C05704-K2, C08972-K1, C09582-K1, C10035-K2, C11332-K1.
Card C12975-K2 was previously compromised in closed case CC-4890 in October 2016 for card-not-present fraud involving unrecognized online purchases totaling $800.03.

Transaction 3660259 in the micro-charge run was executed using device D000168, a generic desktop IE 11 profile associated with 45 cards in the window and 41 historical closed fraud cases including CC-5084.

The micro-authorizations on card C12975-K2 were spaced across 21 days rather than clustered within one hour, and were not followed by a large authorization over $100, which does not fit standard Rule R5 card testing.

Region 337 is familiar to card C12975-K2, accounting for 28 prior transactions (14.1% of card history), and shows no elevated fraud concentration with a lift of only 0.14 vs base rate in the 7-day window.

first.ref: query:policy_sections(section=Section 3a. A case is not a report)
first.section: Section 3a. A case is not a report
first.text: Section 3a. A case is not a report. Two different things, and the agent produces both. **A case** (`CREATE_CASE`) is the bank's internal record of an investigation. Open one whenever fraud probability reaches 0.30, whenever you request evidence, or whenever a customer disputes a charge. A case can be closed as fraud or as legitimate. It can be updated when new evidence arrives. It should be written into the graph so later investigations can find it: a case that names a merchant or a device becomes evidence for the next analyst. **A suspicious activity report** (`FILE_REPORT`) is a regulatory filing sent outside the bank. File one when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected **and** at least one of these holds: exposure exceeds $1,000; the activity connects to a shared device profile, a shared region cluster, or another customer's fraud; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented (rule R9). A report always has a case behind it. Most cases never need a report. The report narrative must stand on its own: who, what, when, where, how, and why it is suspicious. Deciding correctly between ""case only"" and ""case plus report"" is part of the next-best-action score.

steps.detail: Customer C12975 reported unauthorized activity after transaction 3660260 was flagged, uncovering an episode of six online micro-authorizations for product C totaling $23.99 between January 5 and January 26, 2017. These charges represent an unprecedented departure from the cardholder's established baseline of in-person product W transactions. Graph analysis revealed an identical micro-authorization signature across 20 other cards and customers active in the same 30-day period. Transaction 3660259 was conducted via device D000168, which is tied to 41 prior fraud cases, and card C12975-K2 was previously compromised in case CC-4890. The activity was confirmed as an undocumented coordinated micro-billing fraud scheme, resulting in card blockage, scheme monitoring, and regulatory reporting.
